Write the plan.
orch builds it.

orch turns a markdown plan into GitHub issues and builds them into merged pull requests with Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, on your machine and the subscriptions you already pay for.

$ brew install gabrielkoerich/tap/orch
Get started View on GitHub

Works with Claude CodeCodexOpenCodeKimiMiniMaxGrok

The loop you no longer run

Agents write the code. The work is everything around them: splitting the plan, starting each session, pasting the CI failure back, answering the review, rebasing, merging, starting the next task. orch does all of it.

  1. 01

    Plan

    Write what you want in markdown. orch plan turns it into a roadmap and shows it to you first.

  2. 02

    Issues

    One GitHub issue per task, with blocked-by links. A task starts when its blockers merge.

  3. 03

    Agent

    Each task runs in its own worktree, on the agent with quota left.

  4. 04

    Review

    A second agent reviews the PR. Requested changes go back to the author.

  5. 05

    CI

    Your GitHub Actions or shipcheck test it. Red checks go back to the author too.

  6. 06

    Merge

    It merges under your branch protection, and the tasks that waited on it start.

A task marked Owner: human waits for you. Everything else runs without you.

Your machine, your subscriptions

Runs where your code is

A headless service on your Mac or Linux box. Agents run in tmux sessions inside git worktrees that share build output, so a new task starts warm.

Routes by quota

When Claude hits its limit, the next task goes to Codex or OpenCode. Rate limits, expired credits and dead models cool down and fail over on their own.

Nothing to resell

No API keys, no cloud, no telemetry. orch talks to GitHub and to the agent CLIs you already logged in to, and nothing else.

What orch handles for you

Review cycles

Changes requested go back to the same agent, branch and worktree.

Red CI

Failed checks reach the author with the failing tests.

Rebases

A branch that falls behind is rebased, and a conflict goes back to its author.

CI first

A plan for an empty repo starts with a task that sets up its tests and CI.

Your phone

Follow and steer tasks from Telegram or Discord.

Secrets

Agent output is scanned and redacted before anything reaches GitHub.

Built from a plan

brain, a knowledge base for agents, went from one roadmap file to 41 of 47 tasks merged in about 45 hours. The other 6 were marked for a person from the start.

Install

# log in to gh and one agent CLI first
brew install gabrielkoerich/tap/orch
orch init
orch plan PLAN.md
# log in to gh and one agent CLI first
cargo binstall orch-cli
orch service install
orch init
orch plan PLAN.md

orch init finds your agent CLIs and asks for one repository. The rest is in Getting started.

Questions

What does it cost?

Nothing. orch is MIT licensed and runs the agent CLIs on the plans you already pay for. It never asks for an API key.

Is it safe to let it merge?

orch merges only what your branch protection allows. Every PR gets a second agent's review and your CI, and a plan for a new repo sets up CI before anything else.

Does my code leave my machine?

It goes where it goes today: to GitHub and to the agents you use. orch adds no server of its own and collects no telemetry.

Which agents work?

Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kimi, MiniMax and Grok. orch picks one per task by complexity and remaining quota, and a label can pin one.

What does it not do?

Work that needs taste, such as design and copy, stays with you. Mark it Owner: human in the plan and orch builds around it.
